::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 19th [1871]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection C0171: Box 29
:::

My dear [Mrs Valentine](people/person_1437.qmd),
I think this is a very good time to bring forward the [Story of the Crawl](other_books/otherbook_801.qmd) and your pretty ballad shall come in July.[^1] I am sorry it is too late for June.

I am glad you are going to have another annual but I am afraid I am so busy that I have not a scrap available. But I do wish very much that you could persuade [Mr Warne](people/person_1433.qmd) to take those [stories](cmy_books/cmybook_100.qmd) of [Madame Guizot de Witt](people/person_423.qmd)’s.[^2] They have never been published in France and have been most carefully translated. He refused them rather peremptorily last year (not having seen them) from my description but I know I came too late for the Christmas season, and you were away

There are four - on Simon de Montfort, on the childhood of Jaqueline Pascal - on Madame de Sevigné and another on La Vendée, the translation of which is not quite finished. They would make a charming volume.

I am coming to London on Monday and will send the three from the parcels delivery to you - I am really anxious about them, for the sake of sending something to the family - and the tales seem to me excellent

I shall be at [H H Gibbs](people/person_558.qmd)’s, Esq, St Dunstan’s Regents Park, N W[^3] until Saturday, so please send me a note there. I have a little [niece](people/person_1613.qmd) to shew all the wonders of London to, and I cannot much depend upon my self - but if I can I will try to call on you

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: 'The Crawl: A Legend of Tichborne', a ballad, was published in *MP* ns 12 (July 1871).  The subject was topical because the trial of the Tichborne claimant was in progress (10 May 1871-6 March 1872).
[^2]: *Dames of High Estate* (London: Warne 1871).  Valentine worked for Warne as a children's books editor.  CMY wanted to send money to Henriette de Witt who was doing charity work in the aftermath of the Franco-Prussian war.
[^3]: St Dunstan's was a grand house in Regent's Park where CMY's cousin Henry Hucks Gibbs (1819-1901), later (1896) 1st Lord Aldenham, lived.
